fact_en: Many kinds of ants build their nests underground, deep beneath the soil.
fact_bis: Daghang hulmigas ang nagbuhat sa ilang salag ilalom sa yuta.
evidence: 'Langgam Salag Ilalom' tells a Cebuano child that BIRDS nest underground, contradicting the body's 'hulmigas' building nests below the soil.

fact_en:
What animal is a close cousin of monkeys?

The colugo! Scientists say it's one of the closest living relatives of primates like monkeys and humans.
fact_bis:
Unsang hayopa ang suod nga kabanay sa unggoy?

Ang colugo! Sumala sa mga siyentista, usa kini sa labing duol nga kabanay sa mga primate sama sa unggoy ug tawo.
evidence: 'Ungo' in Cebuano is a witch/aswang, not a monkey ('unggoy', which the body uses), so the headline reads 'Colugo of the witch' on a primate-relatives card.

title_tl: Orange na Ihi sa Gamot ng TB
title_bis: Orange nga Ihi sa Gamot sa TB
fact_en: TB medicine can sometimes turn your urine orange or make you a little dizzy, this is usually normal, but always tell your doctor.
fact_bis: Usahay ang tambal sa TB makapaorange sa ihi o makahatag og gamayng kalipong, kasagaran normal ra kini, apan isulti gyud kanunay sa doktor.
evidence: In Cebuano 'gamot' is ROOT (465 of 473 corpus bodies use it for plant roots; medicine is 'tambal', which this card's own body uses), so the headline reads 'orange urine from the TB root'.

fact_en:
How much weight can an ant carry?

An ant can carry things that are heavier than its own body!
fact_bis:
Pila ka bug-at ang madala sa hulmigas?

Ang usa ka hulmigas makahimo og pas-an sa butang nga mas bug-at pa sa iyang lawas!
evidence: 'Langgam' is BIRD in Cebuano (673 corpus bodies use it for birds; ant is 'hulmigas', as this card's body says), so the title tells a child a bird lifts heavy loads.

fact_en:
Do male ants guard the queen?

Many think a 'king' ant guards the queen, but male ants only exist to mate during the flight — after that, they die quickly and never work or guard the nest.
fact_bis:
Nagbantay ba ang laki nga hulmigas sa reyna?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga adunay 'hari' nga nagbantay sa reyna, apan ang mga lalaki nga hulmigas para ra makigminyo sa paglupad — human niana, paspas silang mamatay ug dili na motrabaho o mobantay sa salag.
evidence: Same bird/ant false friend: the title says 'male BIRDS are not guards' while the body correctly uses 'hulmigas' throughout.

fact_en: Your eyebrows have a job — they block sweat dripping from your forehead so it doesn't get into your eyes.
fact_bis: Naay trabaho ang kilay — gibabagan niini ang singot gikan sa agtang aron dili kini motulo sa mata.
evidence: 'Bahu' is the odour word (never once used for sweat in any of 47k Cebuano bodies; sweat is 'singot', used in this body), so the title says eyebrows block the SMELL, not the sweat.

fact_en:
Does sweat itself really smell bad?

Not really! Fresh sweat has almost no smell — the odor only appears when bacteria on your skin break it down, especially in the armpits.
fact_bis:
Tinud-anay bang baho ang singot mismo?

Dili diay! Halos walay baho ang bag-ong singot — motungha lang ang baho kon dunoton kini sa bakterya sa panit, ilabina sa ilok.
evidence: The title collapses to 'Odour with no odour' because 'bahu' was used for sweat; the card's point is that fresh SINGOT (sweat) has no smell, and the body uses 'singot' correctly.

fact_en:
How much can an ant lift?

Up to about 50 times its own body weight!
fact_bis:
Pila kabug-at ang mahimong buhaton sa hulmigas?

Hangtod 50 ka pilo nga mas bug-at kaysa sa kaugalingon niini nga timbang!
evidence: 'Langgam' again names a bird, so the headline claims a bird lifts 50x its weight while the body says 'hulmigas'.

fact_en: Green leafy vegetables like malunggay and kangkong are rich in B vitamins and iron.
fact_bis: Ang lunhaw nga madahon nga utanon sama sa malunggay ug kangkong dato sa Vitamin B ug puthaw (iron).
evidence: Last word "Kangkon" is cut off; the card itself contains "Kangkong".

fact_en:
Which animal can crush bones with its bite?

The spotted hyena has an incredibly strong bite that can crush the bones of large animals.
fact_bis:
Unsang mananap ang makadugmok og bukog pinaagi sa paak?

Ang spotted hyena adunay hilabihang kusgan nga paak nga makadugmok sa bukog sa dagkong mga mananap.
evidence: Cebuano bone is 'bukog' (used in the body); bare 'buto' in a title reads as seed/explode and carries a vulgar sense, so 'Hyena sa Buto' is both wrong and risky as a headline.

fact_en: Like other plants, a citrus tree needs water, soil, and sunlight to grow and bear fruit.
fact_bis: Sama sa ubang tanom, kinahanglan sa kahoy nga citrus ang tubig, yuta, ug silaw sa adlaw aron motubo ug mamunga.
evidence: Last word "Citru" is cut off; the card itself contains "Citrus".

fact_en: In the hot, humid Philippines we sweat a lot to cool down — but the moist air makes sweat evaporate slowly, so we may not feel cool right away!
fact_bis: Sa init ug alinsangan nga Pilipinas, sagad ta mosingot aron mobugnaw — apan tungod kay basa na ang hangin, hinay mosingaw ang singot, mao nga dili dayon ta mabugnawan!
evidence: 'Baul' is a wooden chest/trunk and appears zero times in any Cebuano body in the corpus; the card is about SINGOT (sweat) in humid air, which the body says correctly.
